title: Content Studio: Get more from your videos
summary: Turn videos into clips, text, and images with Zoom Content Studio. Repurpose webinars, demos, and training sessions for social, email, and more with AI-powered tools.
body_markdown:
A[webinar recording](https://www.zoom.com/en/products/webinars/use-cases/webinars/) , product demo, interview, training session, or internal update can hold moments worth sharing in new formats and contexts. \[Backlink added: links the webinar use-case page\]


Zoom Content Studio helps turn[a video from your library](https://www.zoom.com/en/products/video-management/features/video-organization/) or an uploaded file into clips, text, and images. You can review and edit the generated assets, then export them for follow-up, education, internal communications, social channels, and other uses. Webinars are one source. The broader opportunity is to make more of the videos you already have. \[Backlink added: links the library feature page\]


Turn your event recordings into new content


[See how it works](https://www.zoom.com/en/products/webinars/features/repurpose-event-content/)


## What is Content Studio?


**Zoom Content Studio is a** **post-event** **tool that lets you use AI to turn a video into clips, text, and images for use across digital channels.** It gives you a project workspace for creating, reviewing, editing, and exporting assets from one source video.


The source can be a video saved in your library or a new upload. After you choose the video, you select the outputs you want, set the format and tone, and add any instructions. The generated assets stay together in one project, so you can refine them without starting over with the original file.


Content Studio supports several common needs:


- Short video clips
- Blog posts
- Social media posts
- Follow-up emails
- Key takeaways and summaries
- Quote graphics
- Infographics
- Internal recaps
- Learning recaps


Content Studio is currently available as a limited preview to qualifying Webinars Plus, Events, and[Video Management](https://www.zoom.com/en/products/video-management/) customers and may not be available to all regions. Access and pricing may change in the future. \[Backlink added: links the named product page\]


## How does Content Studio work?


Content Studio follows a simple path: choose a video, describe the content you need, review the results, and export the versions that fit your channels.


1. **Choose a video.** Select a video from your library or upload an MP4 or MOV file of 10 GB or less. Clear audio and visuals help avoid project creation issues.
2. **Create a project.** In Zoom Events, open Content Studio, select Create from video, and choose your source.
3. **Choose a recipe.** Pick Default, Post-Event Follow-Up, Internal Recap, or Learning Recap. Each recipe pre-configures the kinds of assets the project generates.
4. **Customize the output.** Select clips, text, images, or a combination. Set aspect ratios, text types, voice tone, output language, and the portion of the video to process.
5. **Add guidance.** Use the instruction field to describe what you want, such as moments that answer a common question or explain a specific topic.
6. **Review the project.** Open the project to see the generated assets and project details.
7. **Refine and export.** Edit an asset, create more content from the same project, and export the approved version.


You can return to a project later to generate more clips, text, or images without regenerating the assets you already have.


## Review and refine your content


Zoom Content Studio is designed to work with the videos you already have. You don't need a special recording setup or a separate starting point. Choose a video from your library or upload a new one, then build a project around it.


The workflow is recipe-driven. You can start from a preset or customize the formats and instructions for each project. A single video can produce clips, written content, and images, with aspect ratios and output languages adjusted for each audience and channel.


Editing stays in your hands. You can refine clips by editing the transcript, adjusting captions, adding text or images, and trimming on the timeline. You can edit text assets directly, and you can refine images with new prompts and save the result as a new asset.


For some clips, Zoom can provide engagement scores that are designed to help you decide which moments to review first. Treat a score as a prompt for editorial attention, not a final decision. Before you publish, check context, accuracy, speaker intent, and brand requirements.

## Should you use Content Studio?


Content Studio may fit if you already have video that contains useful explanations, demonstrations, stories, or answers and you want more ways to share it. Consider these questions before you adopt the workflow:


1. **Video library:** Do you have recordings or uploaded videos that still hold value but get little use?
2. **Format needs:** Do different audiences need clips, summaries, emails, images, or internal recaps from the same source?
3. **Review capacity:** Can someone check AI-generated material for accuracy, context, accessibility, and permissions before publication?
4. **Channel variety:** Will the assets appear on social channels, email, websites, learning platforms, or internal communications?
5. **Editing needs:** Do you need to adjust transcripts, trim clips, add captions, or apply branded overlays?
6. **Language needs:** Would translated versions help people access the same material?
7. **Workflow fit:** Do your teams already work in Zoom Events,[Zoom Webinars Plus](https://www.zoom.com/en/lp/zoom-webinars/) , or Video Management? \[Backlink added: links the Zoom Webinars Plus page\]


> **Key question to ask any vendor:** Can our team turn one approved video into several useful formats while keeping final editorial control?


Content Studio is a practical fit when the video is the source of value and your team needs several ways to package it. It may be less useful when your content starts as static documents, when every asset needs custom production, or when the source video has poor audio or visual quality.


## Where can Content Studio help?


Content Studio can extend a video's life in several ways. Each use starts with the same source but shapes the output for a different audience, purpose, and channel.


**Webinar and event follow-up:** Turn a session recording into clips, written takeaways, and emails that[continue the conversation](https://www.zoom.com/en/blog/zoom-marketing-remix-strategy-lessons/) . Use these assets to[reach people who missed the live event](https://click.zoom.com/resources/post-webinar-action-plan) or to point attendees back to the full replay. \[Backlink added: two links to the Marketing Remix blog and the post-webinar action plan guide\]


**Product and feature videos:** Create short clips that show one capability, a written explainer, or an image that summarizes the key steps. Review each output against the demo so it reflects what the video actually shows.


**Interviews and customer conversations:** Pull out a memorable quote, a short story, or a key takeaway. Check that the excerpt keeps the speaker's meaning and has any required permissions.


**Training and internal communications:** Use the Learning Recap or Internal Recap recipe to turn a training session, town hall, or company update into written summaries, quick reference content, or employee-facing assets.


**Older videos:** Revisit an evergreen video from your library and create new formats for a different channel or audience. Confirm that facts, product details, links, and calls to action are still current before you publish.


Across these uses, the goal is not to publish the same video in more places. It is to give each video a new purpose and a clear next step.


## Content Studio FAQs


### What is a content studio?


A content studio is a product or workflow that turns source material into organized, editable, reusable content for different audiences and channels. It can support video, text, images, audio, or other formats, depending on its capabilities. Its purpose is to extend the usefulness of original material without changing its meaning.


Zoom Content Studio focuses on video. It creates a project from a source video and provides tools to generate, edit, review, and export related assets.


### What does Zoom Content Studio do?


With Zoom Content Studio, you can use AI to turn a video from your library or an uploaded file into clips, text, and images. You can choose a recipe or customize the outputs, including formats, aspect ratios, languages, and the part of the video to process. The resulting assets stay together in one project for review, editing, and export.


You can generate more content from an existing project without recreating the original assets, then export approved outputs in supported formats.


### How is repurposing different from reposting?


Repurposing changes an existing asset for a new format, audience, channel, or moment. Reposting shares the same asset again with little change. For example, a long video might become a short explanation, a written summary, or a quote graphic. Good repurposed content adds context or convenience rather than simply repeating the source.


Content Studio supports this by providing the ability to generate several asset types from one video. You might publish a short clip for discovery, a written summary for readers, and an email for follow-up.


### How should teams plan for extended video use?


Plan with the next use in mind. When you create or choose a video, consider who it serves, which moments are worth reusing, what permissions apply, and which channels you will use. After that, review the source, select complete ideas, adapt each one to its format, and have a person approve it before distribution.


Content Studio's recipes and instructions can help shape the outputs. You still decide what to publish, when to publish it, and how each asset fits your plan.


### How should you measure content repurposing?


[Measure each asset against its purpose.](https://www.zoom.com/en/blog/measuring-webinar-roi-and-impact/) Useful indicators include qualified views, completion, saves, replies, downloads, registrations, return visits, or assisted conversions. The right measure depends on the audience, channel, and next step. \[Backlink added: links the webinar ROI blog\]


If engagement scores are available for a clip, use them to prioritize review. After publication, evaluate each asset on its own goal rather than applying one metric to every format.


## Conclusion


A video can keep serving its audience long after it was first shared. Zoom Content Studio helps you turn a video into clips, text, and images, then refine and export the assets for follow-up, education, internal communication, and social distribution.
